label: copy-phase fed-back v, about to output l (or v)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input is v (99.9% of actives, ~100% of mass). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on any other input token. Within copy-phase v inputs it is selective: it is strongest when the token to output next is l (the bigram v-l in the original; 61% of mass, and the top examples are all ...v l...), weaker when the next output is v (a repeated v-v), and weak and sparse for other next tokens. It also prefers v at original position 2-3 (recall_idx 3-4, ~77% of mass) and almost never fires at recall_idx below 3. The largest activations are v at position 3 followed by l, often with another l later in the sequence. Just being a copy-phase v is too broad (precision 3%). The chosen predicate (v input, next output l or v, recall_idx>=3) gets dev F1 0.59 / mass recall 0.82; low-magnitude actives with other next tokens are missed.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: v, l, -, x, n, e; least: r, 1, j, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: l, v, i, c, 3, x; least: t, b, 0, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, t=12.
